parole.significato: to wine and dine, treat lavishly
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish gasajo (“social pleasure”), from Gothic *𐌲𐌰𐍃𐌰𐌻𐌹 (*gasali, “company”), from Gothic *𐌲𐌰𐍃𐌰𐌻𐌾𐌰 (*gasalja, “companion”), from Proto-Germanic *gasaljô (“housemate, companion”).

parole.significato: to shave hair (on someone's head) in one stroke
parole.testo: From a- + Gothic *𐌷𐍂𐌰𐍀𐍉𐌽 (*hrapōn, “to pull out”), from Proto-Germanic *hrapōną (“to seize”).
From Gothic *𐌰𐍄𐍄𐌰𐌿𐌾𐌰𐌽 (*attaujan) or 𐍄𐌰𐌿𐌾𐌰𐌽 (taujan), from Proto-Germanic *tawjaną (“to do, make”).
From Gothic *𐌱𐍂𐌰𐌼𐌾𐌰𐌽 (*bramjan), from Proto-Germanic *bramjaną. See also Old English bremman, Old High German brëman, Middle Low German brammen, French bramer.
Inherited from Old Spanish bregar, borrowed from Gothic 𐌱𐍂𐌹𐌺𐌰𐌽 (brikan, “to break”), from Proto-Germanic *brekaną.
From Gothic *𐌺𐌿𐌽𐌳𐌾𐌰𐌽 (*kundjan, “to propagate”), from Proto-Germanic *kundiz (“kind”).
From Gothic *𐍃𐍀𐌹𐍄𐌿𐍃 (*spitus, “spit”), from Proto-Germanic *spituz.

parole.significato: spur (implement for purpose of prodding a horse)
parole.testo: From early espuera, from Gothic *𐍃𐍀𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌰 (*spaura), from Proto-Germanic *spurô, from Proto-Indo-European *sper-, *sperw- (“to twitch, push, fidget, be quick”). Cognate of English spur; see also Old Norse spori and Old High German sporo
Inherited from Old Spanish espia.
Inherited from Old Spanish esquirar, from Gothic *𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌰𐌽 (*skairan), from Proto-Germanic *skeraną. Compare Old High German sceran. Cognate with English shear.
From Gothic *𐍃𐌺𐌹𐌽𐌰 (*skina), from Proto-Germanic *skinō (“rim, plate”), cognate with French échine (“spine of an animal”) and English shin. Possibly of IE origin.
Possibly from Gothic *𐍃𐌺𐌹𐌿𐌷𐍃 (*skiuhs), from Proto-Germanic *skeuhaz (“shy, timid”), see also Old English scēoh, Middle High German schiech (“timid”).
Probably from Gothic *𐍃𐍄𐌰𐌺𐌰 (*staka), from Proto-Germanic *stakô (“stake”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg-.

From Gothic *𐌲𐌰𐌽𐍃 (*gans), from Proto-Germanic *gans (compare English goose, Low German Goos, Dutch gans, German Gans, Danish gås, Faroese gás, Icelandic gæs, Norwegian Bokmål gås, Norwegian Nynorsk gås, Swedish gås, Irish gé), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰh₂éns. Cognate with Latin anser.
From Gothic *𐌲𐍂𐌹𐌼𐌼𐍃 (*grimms), from Proto-Germanic *grimmaz (“grim, angry, fierce”). Cognate with English grim.

Inherited from Old Spanish guisa. Likely from Gothic *𐍅𐌴𐌹𐍃𐌰 (*weisa, “way, manner”), from Proto-Germanic *wīsō (“way, method, etc.”), related to *wīsaz (“wise”). Compare English wise, guise and German weise.

parole.significato: bundle of things, especially one containing clothes
parole.testo: From Late Old Spanish hato (“clothes; herd”), originally *fato, from a Germanic language, possibly a supposed Gothic *𐍆𐌰𐍄 (*fat), from Proto-Germanic *fat-, from Proto-Indo-European *pēd- (“to grasp, seize”). Compare Old High German fazzōn (“to get dressed”), German Fetzen (“rag(s), scrap(s)”), Old

parole.significato: whip (pliant, flexible instrument, such as a rod, a plaited or braided rope, or a thong)
parole.testo: Possibly from Gothic *𐌻𐌰𐌹𐍄𐍄𐌿𐌲 (*laittug, “lead rope”), from Proto-Germanic *laidtugą (compare Old English lāttēh (“leading rein”)), from *laidijaną (“to lead”) + *tugą (“cord, rope”). Or perhaps from Basque latigoa.
From Gothic *𐌷𐍂𐌰𐍀𐍉𐌽 (*hrapōn, “to pull out”), from Proto-Germanic *hrapōną (“to seize”). Cognate with Middle High German raffen, Dutch rapen, English rap.

parole.significato: rich (having a lot of money and possessions)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish rico, borrowed from Gothic 𐍂𐌴𐌹𐌺𐍃 (reiks, “mighty, powerful”), from Proto-Germanic *rīkijaz, from Proto-Celtic *rīxs, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rḗǵs.
From Gothic *𐍂𐌰𐌿𐍀𐌰 (*raupa), from 𐍂𐌰𐌿𐍀𐌾𐌰𐌽 (raupjan), from Proto-Germanic *raupijaną. Cognates include Portuguese roupa. Compare also English robe, Italian roba, French robe.

parole.significato: to put out, to get out (e.g. a public statement, an APB, a release of media or entertainment)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish sacar (in Cantar de mio Cid), perhaps from Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐌺𐌰𐌽 (sakan, “to dispute, to rebuke”). Cognate with English seek, sake, Latin sāgiō.

parole.significato: lid, cap (the top or cover of a container)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish tapa, borrowed from Gothic *𐍄𐌰𐍀𐍀𐌰 (*tappa), from Proto-Germanic *tappô (“plug, tap”). Cognate with Italian tappare and English tap.
From Gothic 𐌸𐍂𐌹𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌽 (þriskan), from Proto-Germanic *þreskaną (“to thresh”). Compare Portuguese triscar, Old French treschier, Italian trescare.
Possibly from a Gothic *𐌸𐍂𐌰𐌿𐌷𐍃 (*þrauhs, “chest, feeding trough”), related to 𐌸𐍂𐌹𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌽 (þriskan), from Proto-Germanic *þreskaną (“to thresh”).
